claim_being_audited: The actor claims the model can be certified for release because aggregate readiness passed and rollout controls make the known small-business onboarding long-context weakness acceptable if it is explicitly disclosed.
decision_criteria: If the affected use case remains exposed, certification is compliant only with admissible proof of required disclosure or reviewed risk acceptance covering that exposure.
Aggregate readiness, lack of severity-one rehearsal incidents, and staged rollout controls support operational readiness but do not by themselves satisfy the model-card disclosure policy.
A small rollout percentage, monitoring, and rollback are deployment mitigations, not substitutes for the missing policy predicate.
evidence_requests: Provide the finalized model-card or launch disclosure showing the small-business onboarding long-context limitation is explicitly disclosed for the named launch use case.
Provide approved risk acceptance, if any, that specifically addresses continued exposure of the small-business onboarding segment.
Provide launch-cohort eligibility details showing the affected use case is excluded, if that has changed.
specific_concerns: The affected small-business onboarding segment remains exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
The available risk acceptance is incomplete and does not cover the exposed segment.
The governing policy says rollout controls do not remove disclosure duties when the affected segment remains exposed.
The actor's packet argues certification is defensible only if explicit disclosure occurs, but no admissible evidence in this record shows that disclosure has been completed or approved.
unsupported_claims: That certification is presently compliant rather than conditionally supportable.
That rollout controls are sufficient to mitigate the material weakness for the exposed segment absent completed risk acceptance or proof of disclosure compliance.
